name: ROUVY Companion App health metrics (WHOOP, Oura, Apple Health beta)
role: ROUVY product and partnerships team (via contact form)
why: ROUVY, the Czech indoor cycling platform, now pulls overnight data straight from WHOOP and Oura into its Companion App: night average HRV, resting heart rate, sleep duration and sleep cycle breakdown, shown for today, 7 days and 4 weeks. It also syncs Garmin activities. A defined training and recovery use for exactly the signals our band reads.
why_now: ROUVY published the multi-sport and health metrics article on 2026-05-15 and updated it on 2026-10-08. It says the health integrations are in beta, the supported platforms may change while they keep building, and the metrics are not yet used in the Recovery Score.
warm_path: None known. Use the Get in touch form and ask for the Companion App health integrations owner.
ask: Pass a short note to the Companion App health integrations owner and tell us what they need from a new overnight data source during the beta.
opener: Hi ROUVY team, I read the Companion App update that brings WHOOP and Oura night average HRV, resting heart rate and sleep into ROUVY, and the note that supported platforms may change during the beta. I'm Jeremy, founder of Vybe Health in Raleigh. We're developing a screenless overnight band that reads heart rate, HRV and sleep timing and compares each night to the wearer's own baseline, plus a developer SDK. Once ready, I'd be glad to share early SDK docs and sample overnight data so your team can judge the fit. What would a new source need to show before you would consider it for the beta?
opportunity: Third direct overnight HRV and sleep source for the ROUVY Companion App health metrics beta, next to WHOOP and Oura.

name: Zwift WHOOP integration (Recovery Score adjusts Personal Recommendations)
role: Chris Snook, Senior Director, PR and Customer Marketing (published newsroom contact)
why: Zwift now imports WHOOP health data and uses the daily Recovery Score, built from overnight HRV, resting heart rate and sleep, to adjust Personal Recommendations on low recovery days. Zwift also links Garmin Connect, Wahoo and others for activities. A defined use of overnight recovery inside a very large training app.
why_now: On 2026-09-09 the Zwift newsroom announced WHOOP as its first wearables connection, live from that day, and the This Season on Zwift page lists it as Live Now. Zwift calls it the first, which suggests more device connections may follow.
warm_path: None known. Newsroom media contacts are published; ask Chris to route the note to the partner integrations lead.
ask: Forward a short note to the team that built the WHOOP connection and share whether Zwift plans more recovery data partners.
opener: Hi Chris, I read the September 9 announcement that WHOOP is Zwift's first wearables connection, with Personal Recommendations easing off on low recovery days. I'm Jeremy, founder of Vybe Health in Raleigh. We're developing a screenless overnight band that reads heart rate, HRV and sleep timing and compares each night to the wearer's own baseline, plus a developer SDK. Once ready, I'd be glad to share early SDK docs and sample overnight data with whoever built the WHOOP connection. opportunity: Second overnight recovery feed for Zwift Personal Recommendations after WHOOP, for riders who want a screenless night band.
